body:
I find more details.

I wrote my own dll, which needs Godot API, so I copied the whole folder "GodotSharp/Api" to my dll project folder as 3rd party libs.
My game project imports this dll.
Everything works fine when running in the editor.
When I wanna export, it gives me some errors like "Cannot find the namespace Godot in my dll codes".

Oh well, I fixed.

The thing is, I didn't know that NuGet has godot dll. So I copied _GodotSharp/Api_ to my project folder.

Here is what my own dll csproj looks before
```
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
    <Reference Include="GodotSharp">
      <HintPath>..\Godot\Api\Debug\GodotSharp.dll</HintPath>
    </Reference>
  </ItemGroup>

  <ItemGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Release'">
    <Reference Include="GodotSharp">
      <HintPath>..\Godot\Api\Release\GodotSharp.dll</HintPath>
    </Reference>
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>
```
Notice again, it works fine when running game by the editor.

Now, I change the csproj to
```
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">

  <PropertyGroup>
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="GodotSharp" Version="4.4.1" />
  </ItemGroup>

</Project>
```

It works both in the editor and export.
My problem is solved cause I only need Godot dll.

But, the problem still exists.
When adding some dlls which do not exist in NuGet, maybe _HintPath_ is the only way to add them. In this case, Godot may not find these dlls when exporting.
Or, maybe the macro _$(Configuration)_ doesn't exist or have a value other than Debug and Release when exporting. So the two _HintPath_ I wrote above are not used.
I have not tested this btw.

I would strongly recommend you to avoid referencing DLLs directly, and instead use NuGet packages whenever possible. Using `<Reference>` should work fine, but it's easy to get it wrong.

Copying `GodotSharp/Api` to your project folder is not recommended. As you found, using the NuGet packages is the recommended approach.

The error message you provided (`ERROR: Export .NET Project: Failed to build project.`) is a general error. To find the exact cause, please check the **MSBuild** panel within the Godot editor. This panel will show detailed error messages from the .NET build process.

However, looking at the csproj you provided in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/104910#issuecomment-2774135332, I'd guess it's failing to find the Godot namespace/types because the `<Reference>` properties are only included for the specific `Debug` and `Release` configurations which we don't use when exporting a Godot game.

When exporting Godot games we use the `ExportDebug` and `ExportRelease` configurations. Since you didn't include the DLL reference for any of these configurations, building the C# project will fail. But I still don't think it's a good idea to reference these configurations by name (and we may rename them in the future[^1]).

[^1]: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/96435#issuecomment-2323524064
